title: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war
summary:
Vice-President JD Vance sent shockwaves through Washington on Wednesday by blaming his party's midterm defeat squarely on the Iran war, in what was widely interpreted as an effort to distance himself from President Donald Trump ahead of a potential 2028 White House run.
In a carefully calibrated, 600-word statement on X, the vice-president acknowledged that Trump's 2024 voters had deserted Republicans in the midterm election.
In interviews late Tuesday night and Wednesday, Trump had defended the war but acknowledged that it played a factor in Democrats flipping control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate.
Vance's view on the war in Iran is an open secret in Washington.
But those disagreements had been kept out of the public eye - until now.

title: Why are wealthy countries failing developing nations?
summary:
UN report warns climate adaptation funding is falling far short of needsThe United Nations Environment Programme has published a report warning that the world is not adapting quickly enough to keep pace with the growing human and economic costs linked to the climate crisis.
The UN singles out wealthy countries – responsible for the bulk of carbon emissions – for failing to meet their financial pledges.
At successive Conference of the Parties (COP) meetings, billions of dollars have been earmarked to help developing nations become more resilient.
But only a fraction has been paid out.

title: AP Exclusive: Trump administration held talks with Iran on deporting Iranians during the war
summary:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by The Associated Press show.
The legal group, the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund, brought the lawsuit in which the new court documents were released.

title: Russia to UAE, Iran steps up diplomacy amid Trump threats: What we know
summary:
Share Russia to UAE, Iran steps up diplomacy amid Trump threats: What we know on social mediaIran has stepped up diplomatic efforts amid suggestions by United States President Donald Trump that the US could resume full-scale strikes on Iran.
During the most intense fighting of the war, Iran struck bases in Gulf countries hosting US military assets, as well as civil and energy facilities and infrastructure.
On Thursday, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held phone calls with several Gulf leaders, including the foreign minister of the UAE, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
Iranian officials said Iran has the capacity to strike further than the Gulf using weapons manufactured in Iran.
Control over the Strait of Hormuz has been a main stumbling block in negotiations to end the Iran war since it began in February.
